notes: Session 04 production recipes, consumed by tools/sim/market.py. A recipe runs monthly per business of the named category: output = runs x units_per_run, where runs = workers // crew_per_run (workers = employees + working owner, or the labelled nominal crew for system firms). Inputs are either goods drawn from the business's own inventory (goods_in, per output unit) or a money cost paid from the business account to SYS-MARKET (materials_ncr_per_unit — priced inputs the goods layer does not stock; the rate is a SIM MODEL rate, labelled, in the Session 03 pattern). Production never creates inventory from nothing: every output unit traces to input units or a paid materials cost, recorded in inventory_movements.

recipes.note: Farmland produces from land + paid inputs (seed, feed, fuel). The materials rate is SIM MODEL (no farm input price in prices.json).
River fishing: paid inputs are ice, fuel and net repair (SIM MODEL rate).
The godowns/warehouse mill and pack: one lot of produce becomes one food basket, plus a paid processing cost (SIM MODEL rate).
Factory lots from paid raw material. The 550 rate is SIM MODEL, set against prices.json construction_materials scale (a 50kg cement bag is 550).

Workshops turn manufactured lots into clothing sets, plus a paid finishing cost (SIM MODEL rate). A manufacturing business runs the first recipe whose inputs it can source: factories make lots, workshops convert them.
Packing/repair workshops turn manufactured lots into household supplies (SIM MODEL finishing rate).
